title.en: GSEQ complete elliptic integrals K(m), E(m) approximation

summary: Evaluate the polynomial-logarithmic approximations to K(m) and E(m), with elementwise mathematical endpoint limits K(1)=+Inf and E(1)=1.

identity.relation: K(m), E(m) from nested polynomial-logarithmic evaluation: K = a_k(p) - b_k(p)*log(p), E = a_e(p) - b_e(p)*log(p) with p = 1 - m and the source's hardcoded polynomial coefficients.
identity.direction: squared modulus m in [0, 1] -> complete elliptic integrals K(m) and E(m)
identity.definition: For 0 <= m < 1, retain the source polynomial-log arithmetic. At m=1 set K=+Inf and E=1 for each element, independent of other array entries. This D2 repair replaces the false finite whole-array K sentinel and mixed-array E NaN.
identity.model: source polynomial-log approximation on the interior with corrected mathematical endpoint limits
identity.boundary: Finite inputs in [0,1]; K(1) is a divergent integral represented by +Inf, while E(1)=1. The downstream filament field rejects coincident geometry.
assumptions: The interior approximation preserves the source polynomial-log arithmetic for traceability; corrected endpoint limits deliberately differ from the historical whole-array guard. It is not the most accurate K/E evaluation available.
No external physics reference is bound: accuracy is quantified against scipy's ellipk/ellipe as sampled evidence.

outputs.name: complete_k
outputs.description: First-kind complete elliptic integral K(m), source approximation.
outputs.constraints: Finite approximation for m<1; +Inf at every m=1 element, representing the divergent integral.

outputs.name: complete_e
outputs.description: Second-kind complete elliptic integral E(m), source approximation.
outputs.constraints: Finite approximation for m<1; exactly 1 at every m=1 element.

preconditions: Squared moduli from a caller (e.g. the coil Green geometry operator) in [0, 1].
supported: Polynomial-log K(m), E(m) approximation with mathematically correct singular endpoint values.
excluded: High-precision K/E evaluation (use a scientific library), modulus generation, coil geometry, and the Green field responses.

failure_semantics.invalid_input: Raises ValueError when any entry is non-finite or outside [0, 1].
failure_semantics.runtime_failure: No iterative failure. K(1)=+Inf is the mathematical divergence, not a finite-field result; no NaN or finite K sentinel is emitted at this endpoint.

provenance.lineage_summary: Development integration from the saved GSEQ operator package and its original MATLAB fun_ellipEK apx==1 source anchor. The earlier SciRel implementation followed the MATLAB whole-array guard, producing a finite K sentinel for all-endpoint arrays and E=NaN for mixed arrays at m=1. The current D2 successor preserves the interior polynomial-log arithmetic but replaces that guard with elementwise mathematical limits K(1)=+Inf and E(1)=1. The saved L1 Python operator also used elementwise endpoint substitution; its package tests alone did not establish boundary equivalence. The current correction is supported separately by analytic endpoint identities, mixed-array regressions and sampled SciPy comparison. The saved package remains bounded historical comparison only; no qualified D1 provenance or expert approval is claimed.
source_kinds: saved L1 operator document and implementation

example.description: Evaluate interior approximations and mathematical endpoint limits in whole and mixed arrays.
example.code:
import numpy as np
from scirel.field import evaluate_complete_elliptic_integrals
k, e = evaluate_complete_elliptic_integrals(np.array([0.5, 0.9]))
assert np.all(np.isfinite(k)) and np.all(np.isfinite(e))
k1, e1 = evaluate_complete_elliptic_integrals(np.array([1.0]))
assert np.isposinf(k1[0]) and e1[0] == 1.0
km, em = evaluate_complete_elliptic_integrals(np.array([0.5, 1.0]))
assert np.isposinf(km[1]) and em[1] == 1.0
example.expected: Interior K/E remain finite; every m=1 entry gives K=+Inf and E=1.

scope: Source polynomial-log evaluation against an independent recomputation.
Elementwise analytic endpoint limits and unchanged invalid-input rejection.
verification.evidence_ceiling: Maintained tests establish exact interior polynomial-log arithmetic and unchanged sampled relative bounds 1e-8 for K and 2e-8 for E against SciPy on 200001 points. Analytic endpoint identities K(1)=+Inf and E(1)=1 hold independently of neighboring array elements, and the physical field consumer still rejects coincident geometry. The current endpoint correction supersedes the earlier SciRel whole-array guard; historical source and L1 package observations remain separate evidence. This is not all-input source parity or a continuous approximation-error bound.
known_limitations: The saved GSEQ bundle supports bounded historical development comparison only; qualified-L1 delivery root is empty.
The approximation is less accurate than library special functions (~1e-8 relative sampled); consumers needing higher accuracy should use the baseline scipy-elliptic filament relation instead.
The endpoint correction intentionally differs from the historical source guard; K(1) must not be treated as a finite magnetic field.
Public distribution licensing remains pending a human decision.
